csv_project_name: CMAR for TSU Agricultural Sciences Building
csv_scope_of_work: The Texas A&M University System Office of Facilities Planning & Construction (FP&C) on behalf of the Board of Regents of The Texas A&M University System (Owner) and Tarleton State University, is accepting proposals for the selection process to enter into a contract with a Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) firm to provide pre-construction services such as constructability guidance, cost estimates, and construction schedules; provide a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP); and perform complete construction services consistent with the CMAR construction delivery process as utilized by The Texas A&M University System for the Agricultural Sciences Building (#04-3425) for Tarleton State in Stephenville, Texas. The new four-story Agricultural Sciences Building will house updated laboratory, teaching, student, and administrative spaces for the Tarleton campus, including the four departments of the College of Agriculture & Natural Resources (COANR). The four departments of COANR include: Department of Animal Science; Department of Wildlife & Natural Resources; Department of Agricultural Education & Communication; Department of Agribusiness. The facility will have a total of 113,500 Gross Square Feet (GSF), including 100,500 Priority 1 GSF and 13,000 Priority 2 GSF. The new building is proposed to be predominantly four floors, with heavy traffic and classrooms on the first floor. Offices, smaller classrooms, teaching labs and research labs will be located on the upper floors. Situated on the south edge of campus directly across Texan Trace from the recent Engineering Building, the building will occupy a prominent central gateway location. The site for the new building is at Washington Street and N. Lillian in the current P36 surface lot, as well as the area to be vacated by demolished Ferguson Hall, Bender Hall, and the supporting site structures. It is anticipated that all COANR functions will vacate the Joe W. Autry Building for the new Agricultural Sciences Building. This project will not demolish the existing building, and renovations have been ongoing, though the University has not formally identified what functions will be accommodated in the existing space.
